mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, it indicates a weakening labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate profit growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in consumer spending, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% signals a manufacturing slowdown that erodes corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines >0.5% during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for the signal in that regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand for residential construction, which enhances corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST rises, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% indicates persistent inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL yoy change > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a contractionary monetary policy combined with labor market deterioration, which suppresses corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rise, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 0.5% indicates an economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 declines >0.5% during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC for the signal in that regime is below 0.03.
